newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso gets boost from inflows.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso gets boost from inflows.

text.p: The Philippine peso got a boost on Thursday from inflows of $60-100 million, traders said.
"We heard from the market there was a direct investment inflow," a foreign bank dealer said.

That catapulted the peso to a day-high of 27.65 pesos at midession to the dollar before closing at 28 pesos as some foreign banks took the opportunity to buy up the dollar to cover their short positions, a dealer said.
The peso closed the previous day at 29.30 to the dollar.
The central bank continued to make its presence in the market but its intervention was minimal, dealers said.
"It was just there to set the tone," the dealer said, adding the central bank may have sold only $3 million.
Dealers said the peso may show more stability in the coming days following its de facto devaluation last Friday.
One trader said some offshore funds have started coming back to invest in fixed income securities as jitters in the region's currency markets have started to subside.
